attribution.note: Marcus quotes a passage from his own joint IEEE Spectrum article with Southen and explicitly stands by it, so it is his endorsed claim.

semantics.note: 'It remains to be seen whether' leaves an open question. The drafter turns it into a firmer historical claim that reliability has not been shown. The speaker made no firm commitment that evidence could test.

contract.note: The contract correctly declines the stronger normalisation and treats the sentence as hedged and not scorable. It sets no reliability threshold, test population or horizon.

reviews.rationale: The sentence says reliability is still an open question. It does not commit to an outcome. Under the policy, hedged or open-question language is not scored, and the packet correctly contains no outcome evidence.

attribution.note: Marcus writes in his own voice and endorses the training fact in the parenthetical ('nobody is really disputing this').

semantics.note: An existence claim that some popular GenAI systems had trained on copyrighted images by the time of the post. The normalisation matches the statement.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: one documented, widely used image generator trained on copyrighted works by 2024-01-24 is enough. Licensed use does not count against the claim.

evidence.note: UK High Court judgment, available 2025-11-04, before the evaluation date. It records Stability's admission that copyrighted works were used to train Stable Diffusion versions released in 2022, including v1.4 and v2.0.
Stability's own October 2022 announcement, a company disclosure, reports more than 200k developers and over 1M DreamStudio users. This shows Stable Diffusion was widely used before the post.

reviews.rationale: Stability admitted in court that copyrighted works were used to train Stable Diffusion models released in 2022. Its 2022 disclosure documents wide adoption before Jan 2024. Together these meet the contract's existence test. No counterevidence was found.
